component.name: Pickit
component.summary: Create desktop widgets by describing them

description.p: Describe a widget in plain language, such as a clock, system meters, weather or a now-playing panel. Pickit uses an AI model to build it and pins it to your desktop.

ul.li: Widgets sit on the desktop below your windows, on every workspace, on X11 and Wayland
They stay after you close the app and come back after a reboot
Refine any widget by asking for changes, such as "make it bigger and blue"
Click any part of a widget and tell the AI what to change about it, or edit the widget's code directly
A gallery of ready-made widgets that work without any AI setup
One theme restyles every widget at once, and an inspector changes colors and sizes by hand
Share widgets as files that others open with a double-click
Live data comes from shell commands that you review and approve first
Light on memory: most widgets are drawn natively with GTK
Works with Claude (your Claude Code login or an API key), a free local model through Ollama, or any model on OpenRouter

screenshot.caption: Editing a widget with a live preview
Selecting one part of a widget to change it

ul.li: Approvals are kept apart from the widgets, so a widget file can't approve itself
Optionally run every widget command in a restricted sandbox, away from your files
The approval dialog warns about risky commands, and Settings lists and revokes approvals
On KDE Plasma 6, Show Desktop no longer hides the widgets

description.p: A security release. Please update, especially if you open widget files from other people.

ul.li: HTML widgets can no longer read your files, and can only load fonts and libraries from a few trusted CDNs
Widget files from other people open only after you trust them
Generating widgets with Claude Code no longer loads your Claude Code plugins, hooks or MCP servers
API keys are kept in your desktop keyring instead of the settings file

description.p: Native Wayland widgets: on KDE Plasma, Hyprland, Sway, COSMIC and other compositors with layer-shell, widgets are now real desktop-layer surfaces. GNOME and Cinnamon keep using XWayland, as before.

ul.li: A theme for all widgets: presets, colors, corner radius and font, with light/dark mode that can follow the desktop
A property inspector to change the colors, sizes and text of a selected part without AI or code
Lock widgets in place, or let clicks pass through them
Move widgets between monitors
Undo and redo changes, with the last 10 versions of every widget kept
Rings and bars animate smoothly to new values

description.p: Customize widgets in detail: select any part of a widget in the preview and tell the AI what to change about just that part, or open the new Code tab to view and edit the widget's layout, settings and commands directly, with checks before anything is applied.

A gallery of thirteen ready-made widgets that you can add without setting up any AI, and widget sharing: export a widget as a .pickit file, and anyone can open it with a double-click and approve its commands.

Choose your AI: besides Claude, Pickit now works with local models through Ollama (free, and your prompts stay on your computer) and with any model on OpenRouter. Settings shows the options for each backend and can test the connection.
A new app icon, a neutral background for the widget preview, and a proper monospace font for commands in the approval dialog.

New native engine: most widgets are now drawn with GTK instead of a web engine, using a fraction of the memory (five typical widgets: about 25 MB). The AI picks native automatically whenever the design allows and uses HTML for free-form designs.
Widgets use about 40% less memory by sharing one web process, and newly generated widgets follow performance rules so they stay near 0% CPU when idle.
New media widgets work with any player without extra packages: they read players directly over D-Bus instead of relying on playerctl. Generated widgets also avoid other tools that are often missing.
Fixes widgets with shadows, rounded cards or animations not being drawn in the Flatpak.

ul.li: Widgets refresh immediately on power changes, waking from sleep and network changes
Widgets restart themselves if they crash or stop responding
Widgets no longer appear in docks such as Plank
Only one widget daemon runs at a time, so widgets are never drawn twice
Signed Flatpak repository: install and update from any software center
